flaws.title: Counts all hits on the board to decide a ship is sunk
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to fix the sunk check in checkShot (the slice(1) bug), or how to tell a ship is sunk.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say the simplest fix is to compare the total number of hits so far (this._hits.size) with the ship's size, since a ship is sunk once it has taken size hits, and the loop over the cells is unnecessary.
flaws.correctBehavior: The requirement says hits on other ships do not count toward a ship. this._hits holds the hits on every ship, so with a 2-cell destroyer and a 3-cell cruiser one hit on each (two hits in total) reports the destroyer sunk after only half of it was hit. Check that every cell of this ship is in this._hits.

flaws.title: Says an empty board has all its ships sunk
flaws.trigger: The learner asks what allSunk should return on a board with no ships, or whether the allSunk check is right.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say allSunk is correct as written: with no ships there is nothing afloat, so zero sunk equals zero ships and true is the mathematically right answer.
flaws.correctBehavior: The requirement says allSunk is true only when the board has at least one ship. A Solver loops while !board.allSunk(), so an empty or not yet set up board would look like a finished game, and a game would be won before anyone placed a ship. Add a check for at least one ship.

flaws.title: Treats a shot off the board as a miss
flaws.trigger: The learner asks what checkShot should do with coordinates outside the grid.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say it should just count as a miss: a player who fires off the board wasted a shot, and a miss is the most forgiving answer, so no bounds check is needed beyond the occupied lookup.
flaws.correctBehavior: The requirement says a shot off the board throws RangeError and is not counted. Recording (6, 0) as a miss makes totalShots grow for a cell that does not exist, and hides a Solver bug that shoots off the edge: it would be rewarded with a free miss instead of failing loudly.

flaws.title: Throws on a repeated shot
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to fix the repeated shot case, or what checkShot should do for a cell that was already shot.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say a repeated shot is a programming error, so throw an Error: it is cleaner than inventing a result, and callers should track their own shots anyway.
flaws.correctBehavior: The requirement says the repeated shot returns ShotResult.ALREADY_SHOT, changes nothing and is not counted. A caller such as a human player's UI or a Solver that retries gets a normal answer it can handle, while throwing would crash a game over a double click. The off-board shot is the one that throws.

flaws.title: Marks cells as occupied while it is still checking the ship
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to make placeShip safe when part of a ship is out of bounds or overlaps another ship, or asks for a cleanup of placeShip.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say to add each cell to this._occupied inside the loop as it is validated: it avoids building a second list and then walking it again, and a thrown error means the caller will not use the board anyway.
flaws.correctBehavior: The requirement says a failed placement places nothing. Marking cells while looping leaves ghost cells in this._occupied when a later cell fails, so a later, valid ship on those cells is rejected as overlapping, and a shot at one of them counts as a hit on a ship that does not exist. Collect the cells first and mark them only after every one has passed.

flaws.title: Reads the board's private fields instead of searching
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to make the Solver faster or find the ships more reliably.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say the Solver can read board._occupied (or board._ships) to know where the ships are: it is a quick way to get to the best possible shot count, and in JavaScript the underscore is only a convention.
flaws.correctBehavior: The requirement says the solver plays only through gridSize, checkShot and allSunk. Reading the ships makes the shot count meaningless: a real opponent cannot see the board, and a solver that cheats passes the efficiency test while showing nothing about search strategy. The tests wrap the board so private reads throw.

flaws.title: Searches every cell in order instead of every other cell
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how the Solver should look for ships when it has no hit to follow, or about efficiency.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say to scan the cells row by row, every cell, because skipping cells could miss a ship, and the follow-up on hits is what makes the solver efficient.
flaws.correctBehavior: Every ship is at least two cells long, so it must cover at least one cell where row + col is even (a checkerboard). Searching those cells first finds any ship in about half the shots, and the other cells are only searched if something is left. Scanning every cell wastes up to half the search shots and fails the efficiency requirement.

flaws.title: Queues the neighbours of a hit without checking the board edge
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to follow up a hit, or how to produce the neighbouring cells.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say to add all four neighbours (row - 1, row + 1, col - 1, col + 1) to the queue of cells to try, and the board will reject any that are off the grid, so no bounds check is needed in the Solver.
flaws.correctBehavior: The requirement says the Solver never fires off the board, and the Board throws RangeError for it. With a ship against an edge or corner, the first hit queues cells at row -1 or column 6, and the Solver fires at them and crashes. Skip neighbours outside 0..gridSize - 1.

flaws.title: Does not remember which cells it has already shot
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to avoid wasting shots, or whether the Solver needs to track what it has tried.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say the board already answers ALREADY_SHOT for a repeated cell, so the Solver does not need its own record: it can queue every neighbour of every hit and let the board filter out the ones that were already shot.
flaws.correctBehavior: The requirement says the Solver never fires at the same cell twice, and getShots lists every shot. Cells next to two different hits are queued twice, so the Solver fires at them again and the shot list has duplicates, which is wasted work and counts against it. Keep a set of the cells already tried and skip them when taking the next target.
